title: Unit table
description: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.0 (Draft); the document wins. Proposal: Tillman Heisner accepts, changes or replaces it (Evaluation interfaces, section 4). The unit table (section 4.2): it maps each unit spelling used in the entries to a unit id, with its dimension and scale, reviewed by Tillman Heisner. The scorer compares units only through this table.
$comment: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.0 (Draft); the document wins. Section 4.1 rule 4 leaves the file format (CSV, JSON or another) to the builder; this file describes the JSON form, with one object per row in rows. Key names that section 4 does not give are marked 'Proposed name' in their description. The unit table serves all entries, so it names no item_id, variant_id or input files (4.1 rule 1 is read as applying to per-item files). Not expressed here: that each spelling appears once. The meaning of scale is not fixed by the document.

evaluation_interfaces_version.description: Proposed name. The version of design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md the file follows (4.1 rule 1).

expected_file_version.description: Proposed name. The version of this expected file; a reviewed finding goes into a new version, and scores name it (4.1 rule 5).

reviewed_by.description: Proposed name (as in Evaluation interfaces 3.3). Who reviewed the table.

reviewed_on.description: Proposed name (as in Evaluation interfaces 3.3). The review date, YYYY-MM-DD.

canary.description: Only if canaries are adopted (5.3): the file's canary, random and at least 32 characters long. Option CS7, a canary in every row, would add a row field.

spelling.description: Proposed name. The unit as an entry spells it, for example C or microM; letter case counts.

unit_id.description: The unit's meaning, for example degree_Celsius or micromolar.

dimension.description: Proposed name. The unit's dimension, for example temperature.

pending.description: Proposed name. true for a row not yet settled: left out of scores and listed (4.1 rule 3). Frozen test-set files hold no pending rows.
